title: Book 12 opens: priesthood continued; Levi chosen yet screened for blemish
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK TWELVE. Concerning priesthood.

So then concerning the sacred stole, and indeed also the sacrifices which God was legislating must also be finished upon the perfectings of the priests, it has been said clearly. And with myriad things as many as have been oracled upon them, both concerning liturgy and cleansings, and accurate diligence of the needing to live most lawfully and polished unto intelligible elegance, I at least think it needful also before the others to say that.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?

Cyril: For a dedication to God and chosen out from all the tribes was the one from blood of Levi, and law was giving to the race the needing to priest, God apportioning to it the select prize upon this; yet he was not leaving the sacred-working multitude wholly unexamined, nor was he simply releasing the matter to whoever happened, through at least being from blood of Levi; but he was ordering to investigate carefully and very finely, lest somehow some of the blamed things having happened to be sick be unwilled by God, and make the approach blemished, and only not also, rushing in with unwashed feet into the tent of the witness, he should collide and not willingly. And it has been written thus again in Leviticus: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses saying: Speak to Aaron: A human from your race into your generations, to whomsoever there should be in him a blemish, will not come forward to offer the gifts of his God. Every human in whom there should be a blemish will not come forward, a human blind, or lame, or flat-nosed, or ear-cut, or a human in whom there is in’ (Leviticus 21:16–18)
translator_notes: Ends mid ἐν into §2 αὐτῷ σύντριμμα; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Lev 21 list finished; bodily illness not guilt; spiritual type; bishop blameless
english: Cyril: …him a crushing of hand or crushing of foot, or humpbacked, or white-spotted, or thin-lidded the eyes, or a human in whom if there should be in him wild itch, or lichen, or single-testicled; everyone who is in him a blemish from the seed of Aaron the priest will not draw near of the bringing the sacrifices to the Lord, because a blemish is in him. The gifts of his God he will not come forward to bring; the gifts of his God, the Holy of holies, and from the holy things he will eat, yet toward the veil he will not come forward, and toward the altar he will not draw near, because he has a blemish; and he will not profane the holy of his God, because I am Lord the one sanctifying them.’
Palladius: So then, tell me, is bodily sickness unto a charge for some? And does the Creator write nature even unwillingly corrupted?

Cyril: Well done, O Palladius; for you think rightly. For cause and writing would sometimes become for some who have voluntary the turning-aside of their own mind unto the base things, and who have prized the inclination unto anything whatsoever of the outlandish; but to blame for the sicknesses around the flesh, happening naturally and unwillingly, I somehow think hard and unsympathetic, and not without share of the charges unto left-handedness. So then it is possible from here to think around that, that the creator of the wholes would not have written the nature of a human upon unwilling causes, nor would he as unholy have sent out the one sick bodily from the liturgy arranged with him; but as again from type of the bodily things he thins us down unto more elegant counsels, and under-shows the many-formed of the passions in soul, and gives to think that the matter is God-hated. Or did not also all-divine Paul say that the well-famed vote upon all the marvelled-at things must follow those chosen unto priesthood? ‘In order that,’ (Titus 1:6–7) he says, ‘the human of God may be complete, fully fitted unto every good work.’ (Leviticus 21:18–23) And indeed he insisted that the bishop also must be unreprovable, and very clearly; and in these he was making much accuracy.
Palladius: I say so. And what then would be also the word upon each of the sicknesses just now numbered for us, I would wish, as you well know, to learn.

Cyril: Come then part by part, taking up as in a form, let us say the things going into mind: ‘A human,’ he says, ‘into your generations, from your race, in whom if there should be in him a blemish, will not come forward to offer the gifts of his God.’ (2 Timothy 3:17) Safe the word, bitter the oracle. For the law has been set not against only those then come from Aaron, but it extends unto all the race, and against every priestly blood, and creeps through unto every time. For this, I think, makes clear the, ‘From your race into your generations.’ (1 Timothy 3:2) For always somehow unacceptable to God is what does not have blamelessly. And a time one would not be able to say, according to which the condemned would become dear to him, as rather upon the spiritual sicknesses;
translator_notes: Ends mid πνευματικαῖς· into §3 ἐκτετίμηται; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Blameless prized in Christ-priest race; blind = mindless; lame = weak zeal
english: Cyril: …and rather the having blamelessly has been prized, and sick nowhere the corruption, complete as it were unto virtue, and well-strong unto sanctification, the having practiced well to be well-reputed in endurance, and keen unto continual understanding. Therefore also going against all the race he makes the law upon this, showing forth for himself the sacred and chosen race unadulterated; then as in tribe Levi, and as from blood of Aaron, but now at least as in those sanctified in Christ the great and according to truth high priest, to whom we have grown attached through spirit, shown forth partners and sharers of his own nature. Therefore also having called unto brotherhood those justified in faith, as with partners he rejoices saying: ‘Behold I and the children whom God gave me.’ (Hebrews 2:13) Or did it not seem to all-divine Paul also to attach the word upon this to the person of Christ?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: So then he bars from the needing to priest the one upon whichever of the named, as sick and mocked. For he will not come forward, he says, to offer the gifts of God, a human blind or lame. So then the matter has from itself, even if thought bodily, much the unbeautiful; for with eyes having flowed out, and indeed also a foot not firmly set, not having to walk straight, how is it not better to be still, neither knowing where at all the priest must go, or else to go with laughter, using another’s foot and eyes? But the word of this would not be much. But the necessary unto knowledge and spiritual contemplation for us, come let us say, running under the thick of the history. So then blind he seems to call the very simple and mindless. For what eye is to the earthy body, this also in soul would be said the mind, lit up by the divine light, and opening toward the pure beauty itself, and by the thin as it were and well-turning motions of thoughts leaping up very well toward the accurate in glory, and knowing not to miss dogmatic rightness. This, I think, is the proverbially said, ‘Let your eyes look straight things, and let your eyelids nod just things.’ (Hebrews 3:1) And it has been said somewhere also toward the mother of the Jews looking not rightly: ‘Behold your eyes are not, nor is your heart good, but unto your greed and unto pouring out the innocent blood itself, and unto your injustices, and unto murder of doing them.’ (Proverbs 4:25) So then unsuitable unto sacred-work is the blind intelligibly, that is the wholly ununderstanding, and damaged in mind and sense. And unsuitable besides this also the lame, that is a man not knowing to walk-straight, and not well-strong unto walking completely. For blindness, just as I said just now, is a symbol of extreme ununderstanding; but lameness again, of the as it were broken and weak motion and eagerness which one might make upon each of the things to be done. Unless it is worthy to cry upon those thus damaged (Jeremiah 22:17) (Leviticus 21:18):
notes_covered: Heb 2:13 children; Christ high priest race
translator_notes: Ends mid ἐπιφωνεῖν ἄξιον· into §4 Isaiah quote; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Strengthen weak hands; flat-nose = poor discernment; cut-ear = hard-hearing; crush of foot/hand
english: Cyril: ‘Be strong, hands slackened, and knees paralyzed.’ (Isaiah 35:3) And Christ himself also was blaming the peoples of the Jews, as not enduring to make the tracks upon him straight, but rather turned out unto the lame, and slipped from the reasonings of rightness. ‘For alien sons,’ (1 Thessalonians 5:21–22) he says, ‘lied to me; alien sons grew old, and they limped from their paths.’ (Psalm 18:44–45) So then in equal to one another and very near, as in likeness of passions, are lameness of mind and blindness; the one bringing down unto uselessness the precious as in understanding, the other the well-strong as in good works. And besides these the law said the flat-nosed must be made rejectable, and with him the ear-cut. And one might fit upon them such a word. For by the smelling senses both the foul-smelling and most fragrant are tested, of as many as are in such a nature, the one allotted to smell, I mean; and very discerning is the sense, both of what knows how to delight, and of what not somehow thus, but having otherwise, and as in a worse share; and human mind at least, if it should somehow have completely in the things according to itself, goes well-strongly unto being able to discern the quality of the things, and will make the accurate assay upon each, and like some excellent banker testing all things, and holding the good, and abstaining from every form of evil, according to what has been written, will be well-reputed very much. For it adulterates the as it were shameful and counterfeit of the things done, and would easily accept the beneficial and better. So then snub-nosedness makes clear the not very healthy and completely having as in sense, according to which discerning each of the things best, apportioning the better vote to the best, and the worse to the more shameful, we both are and have been named wise and keen-minded, and what not of such things. For smell as it were leaping up into mind is as it were a real quality of the things thought by it. And the having been cut-off of the ear would under-show, as at least it seems to me, the hard-hearing. For with hearing cut-off, I at least would grant the passion to be the from-part obedient, and not wholly well-reined unto obedience, or else the not being able blamelessly to hear the sacred, especially writings, which indeed some also do, most counsel-lessly turning aside the well-hearing of the soul unto things not fitting. And these would be, according to the voice of all-wise Paul, those itching the hearing, and turning it away from the truth, and lying upon spirits of error, and having inclined unto profane empty-voices. So then the ear-cut would under-show the maiming of the inward and intelligible hearing, and the corruption from rightness unto the worse. But also if somehow a crushing of foot or crushing of hand should be seen present for someone, let him withdraw, he says, and be ranked in equal with the others, this persuading to think the one somehow crushed in foot or hand, yet not altogether sick, (2 Timothy 4:3–4) (Leviticus 21:18–19)
translator_notes: Ends mid ἠῤῥωστηκότος, into §5 τὸν οὐχ ὁλοκλήρως; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Partial crush = careless work; humpbacked = earth-bent; white-spot = shameless open vice
english: Cyril: …the one not wholly able to go unto works, nor indeed having the walking wholly unreproachable, or the energy, the as in citizenship, I mean, and most lawful life. And these again would be either those doing the work of the Lord carelessly, upon whom the woe has been brought through a prophet’s voice, or those pursuing the just not justly, according to what has been written. And observe that to the intelligible and whole lameness, also the moderate maiming of the leg is in equal, and has been reckoned as the same. For to being able to do nothing at all of the good things, the not doing rightly will lie in equal word. And reasonably it would appear in the lameness the not-at-all; and in the crushing the not-healthily.
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And humpbacked, and white-spotted, and thin-lidded the eyes he writes down again as among the most unapproved. And humpbacked we say to be the as it were bent-over, and looking down with mind, and inclined toward the passions of flesh, and fixing the eye upon the earthly things—clear that the intelligible—and going unto this of judgment thereafter, so as to hate being set upright, toward at least the needing to think the things above. And in these would be the charges of the Jews, about whom it has been written: ‘Let their eyes be darkened of the not seeing, and bend together their back through all.’ (Jeremiah 48:10) And white-spotted, the one having the so-called white-spot upon their foreheads. And this sickness blackens in form the look upon the tip of skin. And it takes away from those for whom it should happen to suffer, the even at least being able to escape notice, flowering upon the brows themselves, and hung upon whole faces. So then such a one white-spotted bodily, but intelligibly under-shows the unseemly, nakedly and unhiddenly, and as it were not having a clean face, but the unbeautiful unto life manifest to all, so as perhaps not even to know somewhere the rightly said by one of the wise, ‘Wise will hide their own shames.’ (Colossians 3:2)
Palladius: How did you say?
Cyril: For are there not, O Palladius, myriad as many passions in us?
Palladius: Yes; what then is this?

Cyril: That, O noble one, I say, each is sick what he is sick, but often being worsted by shame toward brothers, he makes in zeal and much word both seeming to be healthy, and escaping notice in evils.
Palladius: You speak well.

Cyril: But if somehow someone should have come unto such shamelessness as to think as nothing also choosing to sin openly, and to spare completely the prizes unto seemliness, would such a one thereafter not seem to someone to have gone far from the sacred and holy race?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then the law calls such a one white-spotted, as not even knowing and enduring to hide the sickness and passion that happened to him. And thin-lidded the (Psalm 69:23) (Leviticus 21:20) (Sirach 20:26?)
notes_covered: crush = careless Lord’s work / unjust justice
translator_notes: Ends mid Πτιλὸν δὲ τοὺς into §6 ὀφθαλμοὺς; PG mid-cut kept. Sirach allusion tentative.

title: Thin-lidded eyes = see yet not rightly; wild itch / lichen / extreme passion
english: Cyril: …eyes, the one least deprived of seeing, yet not having to do this healthily. Of which sort some would be, for whom understanding is present, yet the choosing to think rightly is not seen present. For some seeing, he says, the good, turn aside the inclination of their own wills unto things not fitting; and others, even being able not to be without share of dogmatic rightness, only not themselves damage their own mind, going unto a most unbeautiful hunt of thoughts, and receiving nothing healthy of the glory upon God; of which sort are especially children of heretics, and Jews besides, who believe the Father to be God, yet most mindlessly thrust away the Son who has appeared from him according to nature. Therefore also true upon them is the hymned through a prophet’s voice, ‘Eyes for them, and they do not see.’ (Psalm 115:5) For seeing benefits nothing, unless somehow the seeing healthily should be foreseen for some, just as indeed we were saying justly that both lameness and the crushing of the foot have been ranked in equal word; for it will differ wholly nothing, from not being able to go at all, the somehow not going healthily, clearly the path as in affairs, and the road as in works.
Palladius: You speak well.

Cyril: And a human will not come forward about to sacred-work, in whom if there should be upon him wild itch, or lichen, or single-testicled, or everyone in whom there is a blemish. So then to wild itch must be likened the most outlandish of the passions, poured down upon mind with sharper flows, and going beyond every measure, and having beginning from pleasure, yet finishing unto a bitter end. Or do you not say that for each of the miss-doings both some measure and unmeasure of the evil is seen?
Palladius: How did you say?

Cyril: The one worsted by bodily pleasure—would he not suffer this both moderately and beyond measure? For some are only worsted, and are sick restrainedly; and others also come unto the tip of the evil, and are sick the pleasure raging uncontrollably, so as even to slip beyond the passions according to nature themselves.
Palladius: I understand what you say.

Cyril: So then upon each of the evils the having inclined outlandishly unto beyond word, and beyond measures of the in custom and among many, would thereafter be said the wild itch. And lichen besides, any passion whatsoever, always creeping unto the broad, and having unceasing the increase unto the worse. And the divine law wills that the falling passions must be contracted by us, and led unto the lesser. You will think some such thing hearing: ‘If spirit of the one exercising authority should rise upon you, do not leave your place, because a healing will stop great sins.’ (Leviticus 21:20) For the unreproved of the passions always creep toward the more shamefully having; and they seize heart and mind, and lead unto complete destruction. So then the base must be blamed by us, with the runnings-up unto the better wrapping (Ecclesiastes 10:4)
notes_covered: thin lids = see without healthy sight; heretics/Jews
translator_notes: Ends mid περιστελ into §7 λούσης; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Single-testicled = half-man / soft; may eat holy yet barred from altar; shared weakness warned
english: Cyril: …it of the sobriety in us, and destroying little by little. And single-testicled besides, he says, just as I at least think, the half-man, and as it were cut-off the perfectly manly. ‘For neither fornicators,’ (Romans 6:4) he says, ‘nor soft ones will inherit the kingdom of God.’ (1 Corinthians 6:9–10) And he names such ones womanish, because having obtained a man’s nature they lie about the manly, soft in both mind and body, and willingly bent toward the unmanly and woman-fitting. And it is likely again that the single-testicled also under-shows something else. For it is custom to name a man the well-strong and compacted, and not insufficiently having unto being able to set upright whatever he might somehow choose. And reasonably half a man would be thought the not wholly well-strong, nor altogether keen unto the things fitting him; for it is not fitting for the one lying upon God to bring forward courage cut-apart for him and the well-strong damaged, and as to be weak from part; but to play-the-man and be strong, according to what has been written, having unreproachable and unmocked eagerness. So then unholy admittedly is the one under a writing of blemish. Yet he is not barred from the needing to share the holy food. ‘For he will eat from the holy things,’ (1 Corinthians 16:13) he says, ‘yet toward the veil he will not come forward, and toward the altar he will not draw near.’ (Leviticus 21:22–23) For those still liable to the inward hidden weaknesses unto mind would share the blessing of Christ, and not as in the rank of the saints unto increase of sanctification, and unto firmness of mind, and the remaining firmly set upon all the best things, but as in the manner fitting those sick unto putting away of the evil, and unto cessation of sin, and unto deadening of pleasures, and unto taking-up of spiritual good-condition. For since Christ is a new creation, according to the Scriptures, in this way we also receive him in ourselves through his holy flesh and blood, in order that being re-elemented unto newness of life through him and in him, we may put off the old human, the one being corrupted according to the desires of deceit, according to what has been written.
Palladius: You spoke rightly.

Cyril: So then he denies the practice of the sacred works to those somehow having the intelligible outrage melted-in and irremovable sick; for least holy is what is always sick the grown-on of the passions; but if also for someone of those having blamelessly at least in themselves, and unreproachably unto liturgy, the being sick of these common and not fading passions happens, he orders that he must not be left unreproved, saying: ‘Speak toward Aaron and toward his sons, and let them take heed from the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they will not profane my holy name, as many as they themselves sanctify for me; I am Lord. Speak to them: Into your generations every human who should come forward from all the seed’ (2 Corinthians 5:17) (Ephesians 4:22) (Leviticus 22:2–3)
notes_covered: Christ new creation; put off old human
translator_notes: Ends mid σπέρματος into §8 ὑμῶν πρὸς τὰ ἅγια; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Lev 22 uncleanness; leper and flux barred; types of soul-death and barren mind
english: Cyril: …of you toward the holy things, as many as the sons of Israel should sanctify to the Lord, and his uncleanness should be upon him, that soul will be utterly destroyed from me. I am Lord your God, and a human from the seed of Aaron the priest, and this one is leprous or has a flow of seed, will not eat of the holy things until he should be cleansed, and the one touching every uncleanness of soul, or a human from whom a bed of seed should go out, or whoever should touch every unclean creeping thing which defiles him, or upon a human in whom it defiles him according to every uncleanness of him; a soul which if it should touch them will be unclean until evening, will not eat from the holy things unless he should wash his body with water, and the sun should set, and he will be clean, and then he will eat of the holy things, because it is his bread. He will not eat a carcass and a beast-taken, lest he be defiled in them. I am Lord, and they will keep my keepings, in order that they may not take sin through them, and die through them, if they should profane them. I am Lord the one sanctifying them.’ For those bringing the sacred things, he says, or the things being sanctified by the sons of Israel, as many as they should dedicate unto sacrifice to God, let them not profane his name, bringing not pre-purified, and still having unwashed the uncleanness which it happens to suffer; or let them know that, he says, they will at once pay the last justice. For I am Lord, that is, not a falsely-named god, against whom even if somehow one should sin, nothing will be a miss-deed. For what would even become from us unto wood or stone, to which also the needing to be corrected would follow? So then correcting unto safety of the uncleanness by the very fears, he usefully numbers the manners according to which it would become from us, so that the ministers may know the road of the fairness most fitting them, and through which they would be both acceptable and clean, walking through the life most dear to the lawgiver.
Palladius: You spoke rightly.

Cyril: So then the leprous and the one with flow of seed he both sets out from the sacred liturgy, and says he must become without share of the holy things, until he should thrust away from himself what happened, and become farthest from being sick. And he joins to these, as sick a same-natured uncleanness, the one touching every uncleanness of soul, or for whom if a bed of seed should go out, and indeed the one touching a creeping thing, and of a man having any denunciation upon pollution; not, I think, the law blaming bodily passions, according at least to the true and blamelessly having aim, but as still in types, by the in-sense and bodily things, showing forth the things in souls. So then a symbol of deadness is leprosy; for it consumes and grazes down the flesh, and changes unto the against-nature, and alters the look of the body. And flow of seed is a putting-away of fruit-bearing, nature flowing unto nothing; of which sort also a human mind would be seen carried aside unto corruption and only not being consumed unto barrenness, through at least being able to understand nothing of the neces (Leviticus 22:3–9)
translator_notes: Ends mid ἀναγ into §9 καίων εἰς σωτηρίαν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Hymenaeus/Alexander; unworthy eating; touching uncleanness = shared counsel/deed
english: Cyril: …sary unto salvation; of which sort Hymenaeus and Alexander have become, both thinking and saying resurrection has already happened. And to these would be added those inclining unbridledly toward anything whatsoever of the outlandish, and simply casting aside the fruit of their own mind unto stale and wanton pleasures. So then the leprous and the one with flow of seed, that is, the one held in works of deadness (and works of deadness would be the passions of the flesh), and the one not having the inward fruit-bearing, clearly the unto mind and hidden, uncorrupted, let him withdraw, he says, from the holy things, until he should be cleansed. For as all-divine Paul said, ‘Whoever should eat the body of the Lord and drink his cup unworthily, eats and drinks judgment for himself, not discerning his body. But let a human,’ (2 Timothy 2:17–18) he says, ‘test himself, and then eat from the bread, and drink from the cup.’ (1 Corinthians 11:27–28)
Palladius: You spoke best.

Cyril: So then observe, O Palladius, the accuracy of the law; for it has least gone against only the leprous and the one with flow of seed, but as it were also condemns-with them, even if somehow someone should touch those sick, I mean leprous and with flow of seed. ‘And the one touching,’ he says, ‘every uncleanness of soul, or for whom a bed of his seed should go out, will be unclean.’ (1 Corinthians 15:33)
Palladius: And what damage from this would become for those touching?

Cyril: None at least, according to the word in ready hand. For touch of body will not defile a human’s soul. But the law is spiritual, and teaches us again riddlingly, that unclean in charges of pollutions are those liable to soul-passions. And those touching are defiled-with them, or clinging, clearly according to relation of same-counsel, or same-deed; ‘For evil companies corrupt good customs’ (2 Corinthians 6:14–15); and, ‘No share for a faithful with an unfaithful’ (Psalm 18:25–26); and enemy and irreconcilable to the dark is the light. And true that ‘With a holy one you will be holy, and with an innocent man you will be innocent, and with a chosen one you will be chosen, and with a crooked one you will twist.’ (Psalm 140:3) And that not only being sick the most outlandish of the passions will be all-hard for those sick alone, but also whoever should become same-minded and same-opinioned will be defiled with pollutions not less than those, he showed at once adding, that ‘Whoever if he should touch every unclean creeping thing will defile him, or upon a human in whom he defiles according to every uncleanness of him, a soul which should touch them will be unclean until evening.’ (Romans 3:13–14) And bitter and venom-shooting creeping things we say both to be said and to be those for whom the word would be fitting, ‘Venom of asps under their lips; whose mouth is full of curse and bitterness.’ (Leviticus 22:4–6) And these would be also before the others those twisting the straight things, and sounding into the simpler ones the word that procures destruction, carrying them off toward thoughts not good, and unto glory upon God the
translator_notes: Ends mid τὴν δι into §10 εστραμμένην; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Twisted glory; until evening = before Immmanuel; wash + sunset = baptism / living bread
english: Cyril: …twisted, or also those somehow saying: ‘Let us eat and drink; for tomorrow we die’ (1 Corinthians 15:32); and those dragging out the minds of the more unlearned toward the pleasure-loves in world. And unclean again and knowing how to defile those touching, or going near, according at least, I say, to the law of disposition, are those about whom all-wise Paul also somehow said: ‘If someone named a brother is a fornicator, or a drunkard, or a snatcher, or a greedy one, or an idolater, with such a one not even to eat-together.’ (1 Corinthians 5:11) Or do you not say that most fitting for the sacred and chosen race is the needing not to have become such evils, nor indeed to be mixed-together with those sick?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: ‘So then he will be in uncleanness,’ (Galatians 4:4) he says, ‘whoever should touch these, until evening. He will not eat from the holy things unless he should wash his body with water, and the sun should set, and he will be clean, and then he will eat from the holy things, because it is his bread.’ (Leviticus 22:6–8) And besides these still he denies the eating of a carcass and beast-taken, as able sufficiently to defile. So then see, O Palladius, the putting-away of every filth, and release from charges, not otherwise becoming in us, except through Christ alone, and as in the time of the sojourn.
Palladius: How did you say?

Cyril: That everything before the sojourn of the Only-begotten is uncleaned and still in pollutions, and without share of life, he showed saying: ‘He will be unclean until evening, and will not eat from the holy things.’ (John 6:33–51) Or did Emmanuel not sojourn in the last times of the age?
Palladius: Yes; for clear is the word.

Cyril: And we have been made alive having eaten down the bread, the truly holy and from heaven, that is Christ, the time having come unto an end, and as it were a sun setting, and shutting the measure of time unto evening.
Palladius: Very much.

Cyril: In this way also until evening unclean is the polluted, and without share also of holy and life-making food, waiting the time of the cleansing. And having washed with water and with sun having set, clean, and having as own bread the from heaven. For as it were it has been apportioned to those sanctified through water, as in holy baptism, I mean, the being blessed through Christ; and indeed he himself is the living bread, and he himself again the one having come down from heaven, and giving life to the world. And that the setting of sun would mark the time of our Savior’s sojourn, you will know clearly, with God saying upon the lamb toward the hierophant Moses: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them take for themselves a sheep according to houses, and it will be, he says, kept from the tenth of the month until the fourteenth, and they will slaughter it, all the’ (Exodus 12:3–6)
notes_covered: 1 Cor 5:11 not eat with named brother
translator_notes: Ends mid πᾶν τὸ into next section; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Carcass/beast-taken; alien / sojourner / hireling barred from holy bread
english: Cyril: …multitude of the sons of Israel toward evening.’ For the tenth hour is said according to which Emmanuel appeared to us, toward the evening itself thereafter, that is the end of the present time. And a carcass and beast-taken inject intelligibly the pollution into those touching no less than leprosy; the carcass signifying the perfectly dead and cooled, as in the works according to the flesh, and the beast-taken openly signifying the soul fallen under the devil. And that it is a saving matter to withdraw from a man who has known to think dead things and cooled in mind, and as it were nourishing Satan upon himself (for he eats down whichever souls he should choose)—how would this not be clear to those truly complete-minded, and who have best-studied to go farthest from everything accustomed to defile?
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: And since toward this accuracy thereafter the narrations creep out for us, and the aim of the law would least be for the polluted, yet for those having blamelessly the needing to share the holy and life-making foods; at once he distinguishes the races very well, and who would be those worthy of the blessing, and able to leap through toward this, has been defined; and to whom again the being scared-away from the sacred edibles is fitting, he made clear saying: ‘And every alien will not eat holy things; a sojourner of a priest or a hireling will not eat holy things. But if a priest should acquire a soul acquired by silver, this one will eat his bread, and his house-born, and these will eat of his breads.’ (Exodus 12:6) So then he bars as still polluted and unwashed both the alien and out-of-tribe, that is the one not yet having believed and not knowing the true God. For for those in whom there is not the being bound through the in-spirit and intelligible intimacy to Christ the great and truly priest, how would such ones become sharers of his breads? For we will not give the holy things to the dogs, and no one would cast aside the intelligible pearls before the swine, according to the Savior’s own voice. So then wholly without share is the alien. And he joins to this both the sojourner and the hireling; and these again would be, according at least as it seems to me, those living for world, and citizenshipping for it, and as it were having made the earth a fatherland, through at least thinking only the things of flesh, yet sojourning as it were in bare and only faith, the love unto Christ. And as far as it came unto words, good and fair; but unto works and manners of the true reverence, having stood out very much far. And hirelings again, having somehow chosen even the believing alone not by shame toward truth, but hunting as it were some wage of seeming to be Christians, the pleasing some, and flatteringly running under the cares from those able to benefit them, and making piety a livelihood and a cover of love-of-gain, molding around themselves the fair-speaking as a mask. So then as far as it came unto power of law, (Leviticus 22:8) (Leviticus 22:10–11) (Matthew 7:6) (1 Timothy 6:5)

title: House-born / silver-bought eat; priest’s daughter + alien; regenerated soul warning
english: Cyril: …if the sojourners and hirelings will be arranged with the aliens and as farthest from the holy things, they will be with those; and only not also sick with brother charges, they will justly undergo the same-natured justice. And he said the sharing of the holy things must be released to the household ones. For they will eat, he says, the house-born of the priests, and whomsoever they might somehow buy, saying somehow both acquired and silver-bought and house-born, the genuine in faith, and household in spirit, and bought of a price, according to blessed Paul. ‘For Christ redeemed us out from the curse of the law, becoming a curse over us,’ (Galatians 3:13) according to what has been written.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: And he further orders that also a daughter of a human priest, if she should become to an alien man, she will not eat of the firstfruits of the holy things. So then he has clearly prized the household one, allowing to share the holy things as genuine; yet that for those having the intimacy toward him, the loving to cling to those not household according to faith or manner, nor indeed having grown rich the as it were kinship from virtue, must be very well declined, would not be unclear to those willing to investigate carefully the faith of the sacred Writings. For just as in the already pre-read he was making the leprous unclean, and again upon this the one with seed-flow, and was setting as sharer of pollution and uncleanness upon them the one become near, and as it were joined from touch; thus also here he says the priest’s daughter, even if she should somehow have the holy kinship, will be benefited nothing from here, joined to another, that is to an alien, the nowhere household, nor indeed from blood of Israel. So then the word of the history in these would be. And with the law brought alongside for us unto spiritual contemplation, we say that he says a priest’s daughter, the soul regenerated from water and spirit by power of Christ, and called through faith unto sanctification; but even such a one somehow will be, he says, without share of the holy things, if she should become to an alien human, that is, if she should be joined to some not truly holy, and not having a spiritual relation toward God; so then for bodies the manner of the joining would be bodily, and for spirits again spiritual.
Palladius: And whom do we say have been carried aside unto this?

Cyril: Those whom the solemn word of wisdom was securing, holding thus: ‘Son, let not impious men lead you astray, nor wish if they should call you saying: Come with us; share blood.’ (1 Corinthians 6:20) And we will add also those who having mindlessly inclined away from the right faith, run behind flesh, not accepting the words through the holy Spirit, but having given heed to spirits of error, in hypocrisy of false-speakers, seared in mind. These thrusting aside the intimacy toward Christ have become according to the true to alien humans, and have endured devilish seeds, fruit-bearing in error the of-error (Leviticus 22:11–12) (John 3:5) (Proverbs 1:10–11) (1 Timothy 4:1–2)
translator_notes: Ends mid τὰ πλάνης into §13 ἔργα καὶ ἀπωλείας; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Widow-daughter returns; Synagogue apostasy type; Jeremiah charges
english: Cyril: …works and destruction. So then rejectable, even if somehow a sacred and holy soul should be, leaping upon such shameful pollutions. For altogether unholy is everything whichever should become abominable and polluted, through lying upon base and unholy men. And next to this he at once oracled another law; and it holds thus: ‘And a daughter of a priest, if she should become a cast-out widow, and seed should not be for her, will turn back upon her paternal house according to her youth; from the breads of her Father she will eat.’ (Leviticus 22:12–13) So then the word of the history is clear, I think; but one must go toward the inward and hidden thoughts. For if, he says, a soul should become rejectable as condemned, and thereafter appear empty of a husband, that is of the intelligible bridegroom, having no fruit from virtue; let her make the walking running toward the in beginnings, and let her return keenly upon the house of her own father, clearly through repentance seeking the intimacy toward God, and then she will eat of his breads. And it grieves nothing also to fit the power of the things said to what we said just now. For if, he says, it should happen that a sacred and holy soul carried under under profane men should slip unto wandering, and receive pollution of alien dogmas, and through this become as it were some widow and sent-away from God, yet somehow sobering and learning what she slipped on, let her return toward the Father. For he receives the wandered, if they should appear clean of the unholy seeds mixed into them, if they should bring forward nothing leftover of the abomination of those who led astray; and thus he herds-together with the holy worshippers, setting himself alongside as bread from heaven, the life-making food for them. And I at least think the lawgiver also under-shows something else for us through these laws. For he as it were pre-voices the apostasy of the Synagogue of the Jews, and the justice upon this, and the kindness about to be upon her according to times, bearing unto return by mercy of God, and bringing back unto the in beginning. For ‘A daughter,’ (Isaiah 29:13) he says, ‘of a human priest, if she should become to an alien man, will not eat of the firstfruits of the holy things.’ (John 6:32–35) For as far as it came unto teaching and learning, all-divine Moses has become as it were some father of the Synagogue of the Jews. So then she was a priest’s daughter; for Moses also is a sacred-worker, inasmuch as also existing from blood and tribe of Levi. But this one’s daughter has become to an alien human. For deeming the things defined from God of altogether little word, and somehow neglecting the seeds from above, she has practiced teachings, commandments of humans, and fruit-bears for the opinion-givings of others; in this way God was blaming saying to her through Jeremiah’s voice: ‘Lift your eyes unto a straight, and see, where you have not been mixed; upon the roads you sat for them as a deserted crow, and you defiled the land in your prostitution and in your evils, and you had many shepherds, unto a stumbling for yourself.’ (Jeremiah 3:1–2) But these at least are ancient charges of the Synagogue of the Jews; and brother to these also

translator_notes: Ends mid καὶ into §14 νέα τὰ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ; PG mid-cut kept.

title: New Synagogue charges; Hosea return; holy eaten in ignorance + fifth
english: Cyril: …new, the upon Christ himself. For accepting nowhere the bridegroom from above and from God Father, she gives heed to the words of the Scribes and Pharisees. So then she has become to an alien human, and in this way has remained without share of the holy things; for she did not eat the bread from heaven, that is Christ. You see the charges, and the justice at once brought upon by Christ for those who have thus been impious. So then observe also in what manner they have been mercied, and brought back unto the in beginnings: ‘A daughter, he says, of a priest, if she should become a cast-out widow, and seed should not be in her, will turn back upon the house of her father, according to her youth, and from the breads of her father she will eat.’ (Leviticus 22:13) For widow and cast-out through the impiety unto Christ the Synagogue of the Jews has been shown forth, and has remained in sins, and in having acquired nothing of the spiritual goods, and has continued long times in this. But she will turn back upon her paternal house; for she also will be called through faith toward God; and with us she will inscribe as Father the creator of the wholes, and would become a sharer of Christ’s blessing. This mystery the prophet’s word also will set clear for you; for he said thus: ‘Because many days the sons of Israel will sit, there being no king, nor ruler; there being no sacrifice, nor there being an altar, nor priesthood, nor clear things; and after these the sons of Israel will turn, and will seek the Lord their God and their king, and will be amazed upon the Lord, and upon his goods, upon last of the days.’ (Hosea 3:4–5)
Palladius: True is the word.

Cyril: So then edible and well-fitting toward sharing for those having undamaged at least upon themselves are the sacred things, that is the holy things. But they will no longer be set forward for those not having healthily, or polluted out by relation toward others. For it has been written that ‘With a crooked one you will twist.’ (1 Corinthians 10:18) And that also for the truly sacred it is not without damage to make the holy things as in common use, and to think them differing nothing from the others, he was clarifying saying at once: ‘And a human who if he should eat the holy things according to ignorance, will also add his fifth upon it, and will give to the priest the holy, and will not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they themselves take away for the Lord, and they will bring upon themselves lawlessness of a miss-deed in their eating their holy things; because I am Lord the one sanctifying them.’ (Psalm 18:26)
Palladius: I do not very much understand what ever it is you say.

Cyril: You will learn also very clearly; for nothing is uphill. The things dedicated unto a smell of fragrance, somehow calves, or a sheep, were being brought up from part upon the altar, with the inwards being taken out, feet, and head, and fat, sometimes also kidneys; and they were nourishing the priests with the leftovers. ‘For those eating the sacrifices are partners of the altar,’ (Leviticus 22:14–16) just as also the
translator_notes: Ends mid καθὰ καὶ ὁ θε into §15 σπέσιος ἔφη Παῦλος; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Eli’s sons; ignorance vs insolence; priests and deadness; pitch-touch begins
english: Cyril: …all-divine Paul said. So then there was a necessity that what is under the brought-forward be consecrated to God, according to the law fitting each, and that the servants be comforted with the remaining body of the sacrifice. But if somehow someone should appropriate as it were wholly through-and-through the gift, and has apportioned it to his own needs, having burned-fragrance nothing; as having eaten down holy things, he was being written by law. This indeed the sons of Eli the priest have done, snatching before sacrifices and profaning the sacred things, and saying most unholily to those come unto sacrificing: ‘Give meat to roast for the priest.’ (Leviticus 21:1–6) But those at least as voluntary and having naked the insolence were being punished proportionally. ‘But if somehow it should become, he says, either having been snatched-together by forgetfulness, or not accurately knowing what seems to the laws, to do some such thing; let him undergo damage; and let him pay the equal without neglect; and let him further bring upon this also the fifth,’ (1 Corinthians 10:18) that is, the fifth share of the valuation; ‘and thus he will be released the charges, and will thrust away the harms from the ignorance.’ (1 Samuel 2:12–17) So then when the unknown is not free of writing, what would one think the from mindlessness and boldness? So then those for whom the sacred things are in care must decline seeking to appropriate nothing before sacrifice; or let them know that having miss-done terrible things, they will owe justice, and will be under divine motion. Or do you not say the matter is true, O friend?
Palladius: Altogether so.

Cyril: And that those priesting must be holy and washed-out, and shake off also very youthfully the as it were dead and cooled mindset, and the not breathing unto virtue, he was making clear saying: ‘Speak to the priests the sons of Aaron, and you will say toward them: In the souls they will not be defiled in their nation, but either in the household nearest them, upon father and mother, and sons and daughters, upon a brother, and upon a virgin sister drawing near him, the one not given out to a man, upon these he will be defiled. He will not suddenly be defiled in his people unto his profaning. And you will not shave a baldness the head upon a dead, and they will not shave the look of the beard, and upon their fleshes they will not cut cuttings. They will be holy to their God, and will not profane the name of their God; for the sacrifices of Lord gifts of their God they themselves offer, and they will be holy.’ (Leviticus 22:14) For no pollution at all would become for a man, the death of another, if one should carefully investigate the word of the truth. Yet bodily deadness would be a type of the inward and in souls, by which the one become near must be defiled, either according to will, or according to same-deed; for to withdraw from dead works and to be borne as farthest would be fitting for saints, and not to go unto the same with those sick such things is beautiful. For it has been written that ‘The one touching pitch, (Sirach 13:1)
translator_notes: Ends mid πίσσης, into §16 μολυνθήσεται; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Near kin mourning allowed; no Greek cuttings; priest marriage bans begin
english: Cyril: …will be polluted.’ For the one not declining to cling would share also very easily another’s baseness. And the law allows those sanctified, upon father and mother, children and brothers, and indeed also near-kin, to be defiled unreproachably; through also going upon soulless bodies, by shame toward nature, and neglecting the injustices unto type, so that those known to God may not seem to be some untearable and haughty and unsympathetic; and indeed with the law saying clearly: ‘Honor your father and your mother, in order that it may become well for you.’ (Sirach 13:1) And according to another manner and word, we say those sanctified have been barred from the needing to mourn; for being sacred-workers of life, and bringing forward the sacred things to God unto the loosing of death (for loosing of death is the death of Christ, being typed through sheep and calves), how was it consistent to be weighed down by griefs upon death? Thus also all-divine Paul writes clearly to those baptized unto Christ unto hope of life and resurrection: ‘And this I say, in order that you may not grieve, just as also the rest who do not have hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, thus also God will lead those having slept through Jesus with him, and will raise with us.’ (Exodus 20:12) So then the law allowed those sanctified to go upon those very near dead. And he measures the matter, and does not allow to loosen what is most fitting them by the excess and beyond need, so that the solemn prize of priesthood may not be wronged. For he sets them out from being made bare the heads according to likeness of the others, and from being scraped the beard upon insolence of face; and the unholy-works of Greek madness, I mean the cuttings unto flesh, he orders not even so much as to take into mind. For to be disposed-together with the household ones unto griefs is nothing unfitting; yet to be altogether unseemly would be unbeautiful and thoroughly struck. ‘For all things,’ (Leviticus 21:5–7) he says, ‘let them become seemly and according to order.’ (1 Thessalonians 4:13–14) And having prized the things of God before; and of the unto parents themselves, according to the ancient law, the Savior himself also has ordered us to lead, saying thus: ‘The one loving father or mother over me is not worthy of me.’ (1 Corinthians 14:40)
Palladius: You spoke well.

Cyril: So then least does he order the priests to need to be defiled upon dead. And showing forth also according to other manners for us that the holy is irreconcilable and unclear with the profane, he was setting for us the laws upon marriages, at once adding: ‘Upon every priest, a prostituted and profaned woman they will not take, and a woman cast out by her husband they will not take; because he is holy to Lord his God, and you will sanctify him; the gifts of Lord your God, this one offers; he will be holy, because holy am I Lord the one sanctifying them.’ (Matthew 10:37) So then the truly prostituted and polluted woman is sick the charge clothed upon shameful things, and has undisputed
