translator_notes: Ends mid ἀναμφίλογον into §17 ἔχει τὴν κατάῤῥησιν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Cast-out wife; Synagogue fornication burned; high priest Aaron = Christ image
english: Cyril: …the denunciation. And the cast-out is nowhere unchargeable. For she would not suffer without cause the needing to be shaken off from the hearth of the one being with her. Therefore those led unto the thus solemn liturgy must not somehow only hold off from evils having upon themselves the most manifest and uncovered condemnation, but also from every deed, I think, to which a reputation of baseness would follow, and a not-good suspicion, and the unseemly in very many suspicions. And the word seems also to hint the misfortune of the Synagogue of the Jews, which, because she has prostituted unto many shepherds, according to what has been written, Christ the all-pure priest did not accept unto spiritual partnership, the one dedicating himself as it were some exceptional gift over us to the Father, the holy with us according to the human, though he himself sanctifies all the creation, as from God and God. And he was finishing a clearer showing of the mystery saying: ‘And a daughter of a human priest, if she should be profaned of prostituting out, she herself profanes the name of her father; she will be burned upon fire.’ (Leviticus 21:7) For she has been given unto flame, as unholy and profane, the Synagogue of the Jews, following the opinions of the Scribes and Pharisees, and dedicating her whole mind to commandments of humans. Therefore also very justly she was hearing the prophet saying: ‘How did you become a prostitute, faithful city Zion, full of judgment?’ (Leviticus 21:9) So then having prostituted out, and having altogether neglected the from-above and spiritual bridegroom, she has become food of fire. Therefore also prophet Jeremiah dripping a bitter tear upon her says: ‘A beautiful olive well-shaded in look the Lord called your name; unto a voice of her circumcision, fire was kindled upon her; great the affliction upon you. Her branches were made useless, and Lord of the powers who planted you spoke evils upon you.’ (Isaiah 1:21) So then a manner of the intelligible prostitution is the inclining away from rightness, and seeking to lie upon shameful and unholy teachers.
Palladius: Thus I say.

Cyril: And dimmer than the things said are the types, and not very clear upon at least the other priests, yet they shine up as it were in Aaron bearing an image of Christ. For he said again: ‘And the great priest from his brothers, of the oil of the anointed having been poured upon the head, and having been perfected to put on the garments, will not un-turban the head,’ (Jeremiah 11:16) or will not un-mitre, ‘and will not tear apart the garments, and upon every soul having died will not enter, upon his father nor upon his mother will not be defiled, and from the holy things will not go out, and will not profane the sanctified of his God because the holy anointed oil of his God is upon him. I am Lord. This one will take a virgin woman from his race, but a widow and cast-out and profaned and prostitute, these he will not take, but either a virgin from his people he will take as wife. And he will not profane his seed in his people (Leviticus 21:10–15).
translator_notes: Ends mid ἐν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ. into §18 Ἐγὼ Κύριος; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Aaron typed Christ; unceasing priesthood; life does not tear garments for dead
english: Cyril: I am Lord the God, the one sanctifying them.’ You see clearly as still in types Emmanuel and Christ, named as in Aaron. For he was anointed with Spirit, according to the Scriptures, himself existing the all-perfect priest. Therefore also he has irremovable the glory of priesthood. ‘For he will not un-turban,’ (Mark 5:39) he says, ‘the head,’ that is, he will not cast off the sacred-fitting shape. For it has been said toward the Savior and Redeemer of the wholes: ‘You are a priest unto the age according to the order of Melchizedek. –And the more are priests having become, through being hindered by death to remain; but this one through his remaining unto the age has untransferable the priesthood. Whence also unto the complete he is able to save those approaching God through him;’ (Leviticus 21:10–15) for all-divine Paul has written thus. So then the not taking away the turban from the head would under-show the irremovable of the priesthood. And if somehow it should be said, ‘He will not un-mitre the head,’ (John 11:35) you will understand very well the continual and unshakeable of his kingdom; for a mitre having the golden bracelet upon tip foreheads would be a symbol of rule and kingdom. But, ‘Nor will he tear apart the garments,’ (Hebrews 7:17) he says. This indeed is custom for some to do upon dead; but the matter is altogether alien to Christ. For life would least suffer the pain upon death. For nothing at all for it is the dead, but it itself is both loosing of death, and overturning of corruption. And indeed also the Savior was sometime blaming those willing to wail the little girl of the synagogue-ruler, ‘Withdraw,’ saying, ‘and do not weep for the little girl has not died, but sleeps.’ (Hebrews 7:23–25) For truly outlandish is their tear-flowing as upon a dead girl, with the life of the wholes present, that is, Christ. And if he has wept upon Lazarus, we say the matter is a fruit of affection, and the sympathetic of the divine gentleness upon us; for nature tyrannized by death was being mercied, and the tear was for it a loosing of the passion.
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And that according to no manner is the profane in Christ, is sidewise under-signaled through saying the high priest must stand away from deadness, going upon no dead at all, with even the honor unto father and unto mother and brothers neglected in this. For see how mindful is the law, and setting in no small word the good-order fitting the thoughts. For upon the other priests he was being shamed by nature, and to those very near and from blood dead he was giving those sanctified to do the customary things unreproachably. And he has not very much cared for the sin unto the shadow. For the charges have been written upon us, and the type unto humans, for whom even if some pollution should follow alongside, nothing unfitting. ‘For we all stumble many things’ (James 3:2); and the miss-doing is sick in us by nature. But upon at least the great high priest, that is, Christ,
notes_covered: other priests vs Christ type purity
translator_notes: Ends mid Χριστοῦ, into §19 τετήρηται καθαρῶς; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Christ without sin; virgin Church vs cast Synagogue; no steps on altar
english: Cyril: …the reverence has been kept purely even in the type itself, and the unadulterated in shadows, in order that the beauty of the truth may not be counter-signed, as wronged in those. For Christ is unprofane, and not knowing sin, and beyond every pollution, rather of intelligible brightness and purity; and inside every sanctification, even if having the clear in this fading, through at least being firmly set by natural laws, and always having according to the same and likewise. And this, I think, makes clear the, ‘From the holy things he will not go out, and will not profane the sanctified of his God.’ (Leviticus 21:12–14) And that a virgin woman must be borne toward partnership of marriage, he says very well, and he makes the cast-out unfitting. Who also would be unto a type of the Synagogue of the Jews; for she has been cast out from the unity toward him, and about her he says through the prophet’s voice that ‘She is not my woman, and I am not her man.’ (2 Corinthians 5:21) And Paul fitted the Church from nations, a pure virgin to Christ, spotless and wrinkleless, rather holy and blameless. Thus at least upon both the Church from nations and the mother of the Jews, the riddle would be true, and the type not unbeautiful. And if somehow someone should wish to turn around the power of the thoughts worthily toward the word upon each, we say that Christ is unjoined to profane and unholy souls; but with the all-pure and clean, as it were virgins, he is with them spiritually, and finishes them fruitful, and calls them own race. ‘For whoever should do the will of my Father,’ (Hosea 2:2) he says, ‘the one in the heavens, this one is also my brother, and my sister, and my mother.’ (2 Corinthians 11:2)
Palladius: You spoke rightly.

Cyril: So then of what sort those chosen unto sacred-work must be, and what things they must rightly hurry to do, and from what things it would be fitting they have been released, he has oracled clearly; but somehow beside this it was wise to say openly in what manner they must sacred-work, and to rhythm by laws both the forms of the sacrifices and every sacred-worked thing, so that the deed may have blamelessly for them, and thus they may make the liturgy most dear. So then also before the others, ‘You will not go up,’ (Matthew 12:50) he says, ‘in steps upon my altar, in order that you may not uncover your unseemliness upon it.’ (Ephesians 5:27) But how somehow would this become, someone will say at once, and indeed he was giving the priests the around-leg made from linen, ‘in order that it may cover,’ (Exodus 20:26) he says, ‘unseemliness’ (Exodus 28:42) of his skin? If then somehow also they must leap through high, the matter would have wronged them nothing having been wrapped the unseemly. So then where then do we say the aim of the law is? For the worshippers of the idols it was seeming both well-famed and necessary that altars be founded high for the precincts; and not much for them was the word upon the needing to be solemnly wrapped.
translator_notes: Ends mid περιεστάλθαι λόγος. into §20 Εὐφυῶς οὖν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Humility not steps; perpetual altar fire; Emmanuel typed as altar
english: Cyril: So then the law cleverly, from what is accustomed to happen for them, sets upright the divine sacred-workers toward the better, and as from a bodily type, leads unto spiritual contemplation. For ‘You will not go up,’ (Hebrews 13:10) he says, ‘in steps upon my altar, in order that you may not uncover your unseemliness upon it.’ (Exodus 20:26) That is, Let the divine sacred-worker sanctified toward my liturgy seek the low things, let him not leap up toward the high. Let him decline boastfulness, in order that he may not be seen unseemly and unbeautiful. For unbeautiful and thoroughly unseemly and all-hard is a sickness of mind, the oversized mindset. ‘For as great as you are,’ he says, ‘by so much humble yourself, and before Lord you will find grace.’ (Sirach 3:18) And the Savior’s disciple also writes: ‘Let the lowly brother boast in his height; and the rich, in his humiliation.’ (James 1:9–10) For he will pass also in equal to grasses, and will differ from flowers of the fields according to no manner.
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: So then he said the sacred-worker must have been released from bulk and disdain. And in what manner he would make the sacred-work most lawful and unreproved, you will know altogether clearly; for it has been written in Leviticus: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying: Charge Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the whole-burnt-offering, this the whole-burnt-offering upon its burning upon the altar the whole night until morning; and the fire of the altar will be burned upon it, will not be quenched; and the priest will put on a linen tunic, and will put on a linen around-leg around his body, and will take away the burnt-consumption, which the fire should consume, the whole-burnt-offering from the altar, and will set it alongside near the altar, and will put off his stole, and will put on another stole, and will carry out the burnt-consumption outside the camp unto a clean place; and fire upon the altar will be burned upon it, and will not be quenched; and the priest will burn upon it woods morning by morning, and will pile upon it the whole-burnt-offering, and will put upon it the fat of the salvation and fire through all will be burned upon the altar, will not be quenched.’ (Leviticus 6:8–13) So then continual and thoroughly unceasing is the fire of the altar, and not foreign or from outside, but its own, that is, the from above and from heaven. And what then is this? For full of the glory of God is our holy altar. And in a form of the fire the divine and unspeakable nature is imaged. And the word seems also very well to under-show something mystical.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?

Cyril: Or were we not saying Emmanuel himself to be the divine, as in type, altar, through whom we approach God and Father, worshipping rationally, and only not sacrificing the fragrant in virtues, and the sanctification of the Gospel citizenship? ‘For present your bodies, a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, your rational worship.’ (Romans 12:1)
translator_notes: §20 closes a rhetorical unit on altar fire/Emmanuel; next slice continues.

title: Altar fire unquenched = Spirit remaining on Christ; ash by sanctified only
english: Palladius: We were saying; for I will remember.

Cyril: See then that fire having come down from heaven upon the altar does not allow ending, nor as it were to stand off having been quenched, but both to be through all for it, and unceasingly to dwell-in. And the Baptizer John also has witnessed concerning Christ: ‘That I have beheld the Spirit coming down from heaven in form of a dove, and it remained upon him. And I,’ (John 1:32–33) he says, ‘did not know him; but the one who sent me to baptize, he himself said to me: Upon whomsoever you should see the Spirit coming down from heaven, and remaining upon him, this one is the one baptizing in the holy Spirit.’ (John 1:26–27) So then the holy Spirit was being typed as still in shadows, coming down in form of fire upon Christ, and always remaining upon him. For unrested and wholly unending is the fire of the altar. And that the Spirit is likened to the nature of fire, the blessed Baptizer also certifies you saying to the Jewish crowds: ‘I baptize in water, but in midst of you has stood one whom you do not know, the one coming behind me, of whom I am not worthy that I should loose the strap of his sandal.’ (Matthew 3:11) And he said that ‘He himself will baptize you in holy Spirit and fire.’ (Malachi 3:2–3) For we have been baptized not into sensible fire, but in holy Spirit, melting out after the manner of fire the pollution in souls; therefore also it has been written concerning Christ that ‘Behold he goes in as fire of a furnace, and as herb of washers; and he will sit melting and cleansing, as the silver and as the gold.’ (Romans 12:1) So then unquenchable is the fire of the altar. For the holy Spirit has remained in Christ, though by nature existing in him, inasmuch as he is thought and is God. And law also said the fire is own of the altar. For even if the Only-begotten has become human, and according at least to the fitting shape for humanity is also said to have come into sharing of Spirit; yet still of him and in him, and truly own is the Spirit. And if somehow someone should choose to lead the word upon this also upon each of those sanctified through faith in Christ, so as somehow already for him also to be thought a divine altar; beneficial is the word; for it is fitting that sacred men, and those having dedicated their own life to Christ, be seen hot and boiling with the Spirit, and this through all, not being carried down unto cooling through worldly pleasures, but rather rekindling the mind in sanctification unto God-love and desire of virtue. For this is the manner of the rational worship. So then this is the word of the altar. And he further orders something useful also for the history. For the ash must be carried out, he says, not by another of the aliens, or being from another tribe, but rather through ministry of those sanctified. And observe how the law leaves nothing of the things come unto divine liturgy to be thought short, nor as it were unworthy of priestly self-working, so as to yield to another not sacred; for the holy things are not walkable for the unclean. And untouched also is the divine (Leviticus 6:10–11)
translator_notes: Ends mid τὸ θεῖον into §22 ἐστι θυσιαστήριον; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Change garments for ash; Ezekiel chambers; perpetual whole-burnt; meal offering begins
english: Cyril: …is altar. And in order that those chosen unto sacred-work may know the beyond-nature of the divine altar as in sanctification, he also kindles reverence for them by the sacred-fitting garments. For he does not allow, economically, those arrayed sacredly to appear outside the tent. For the sanctified things, he says, not having associated with the unclean, and having the pollution from foreigners, must not wrong the reverence of the holy tent. Therefore he allows gathering the ash while arrayed sacred-fittingly, but to change garments when bearing toward the outside, and departing from the holy places. And he has oracled something kin to such also through Ezekiel’s voice; and he writes thus: ‘And he said toward me: The chambers toward the north, and chambers toward the south, the ones being according to face of the intervals, these are the chambers of the holy, in which the priests will eat there, the sons of Zadok, the ones drawing near toward Lord into the Holy of holies, and there they will set the Holy of holies and the sacrifices, and the things over sin, and the things over ignorance; because a place is holy. No one will enter except the priests; they will not go out from the court of the holy into the outer court, in order that through all those bringing near may be holy, and may not touch their array, in which they liturgize in them, because they are holy; and they will put on other garments whenever they touch the people.’ (Ezekiel 42:13–14) So then holy also are the garments of the priests themselves, and unmixed with the many. And in night and day is the whole-burnt; for unceasing is the fragrance of Christ; and the life of the saints itself, if thought as in the manner according to whole-burning, has unpausing the good-smell; for they fragrance Christ, sacred-working to God the boasts as from works of the Gospel citizenship.
Palladius: True is the word.

Cyril: So then in what manner the matter of the whole-burning will be, through what we said, is not unclear. And how the manner of the sacrifice also would become very rightly, he orders saying: ‘This is the law of the sacrifice, which the sons of Aaron will bring it before Lord, opposite the altar; and he will take away from it with the handful from the fine flour of the sacrifice with its oil, and with all its frankincense the things being upon the sacrifice. And he will bring up upon the altar a fruit smell of fragrance, its memorial to the Lord. And what has been left from it Aaron and his sons will eat. Unleavened will be eaten in a holy place; in the court of the tent of the witness they will eat it; it will not be cooked leavened; a portion I gave it to them from the fruits of the Lord. Holy of holies it is, just as the of sin, and just as the of trespass. Every male of the priests will eat it. Eternal lawful into your generations from the fruits of the Lord; everyone who if he should touch them will be sanctified.’ (Leviticus 6:14–18) So then the whole-burnt things under-show the as it were complete and altogether dedication of the exceptionally holy; but sacrifice, itself as from (2 Corinthians 2:15)
translator_notes: Ends mid ὡς ἐκ into §23 μέρους; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Partial holy life = fine flour handful; unleavened; male priests eat; softness barred
english: Cyril: …part holy and under God life; of which an accurate under-typing is the fine flour brought up through a priest’s handful with the oil and the frankincense. For the life being consecrated to God, even if it should somehow become from part, must be wholly fragrant, and being fattened with most rich hopes. Or do you not say every good work of ours is most sweet-smelling?
Palladius: Very much so.
Cyril: And what? Is it not done by us upon good hopes?
Palladius: Yes; for the things from God will wholly follow.
Cyril: So then frankincense, and fine flour oil-wet, under-hints for us the fragrant and most rich life.
Palladius: You spoke well; but what would the as-from-part holy life become by us?

Cyril: The one neither having come unto a leaving-off of the sacred-fitting citizenship, nor going according to the very withdrawn path, of which sort somehow was John’s voice, or of the holy apostles; nor indeed falling out of being revered, through somehow having been worsted of the very underlying. Or is not the life of those in world and child-begetters, if they should choose to live through well, somehow shared to God and world, according to blessed Paul’s voice?
Palladius: It has been shared; for how not?

Cyril: So then a type of life not altogether dedicated to God, but as it were middle and looking upon both, was the partial consecration of the fine flour, having the fragrant and cheerful; which also the law says will be unto memorial of the one having brought through priestly service. And we will truly gain the lying in memory with God, through the things by which fruit-bearing we fragrance; with Christ mediating and bringing near to God, the one wholly holy, as in rank of the whole-burnt offerings; and indeed the one not such altogether through having been shared to the world, as it were some partial sacrifice. And unleavened is the sacrifice. For it would be fitting that everything whichever should become by us unto glory of God be done purely. And indeed the Savior has ordered to decline standing in mid markets making the prayers, and the unsmiling in fasts, and trumpeting disorderedly when pitying brothers. For this is leaven, profaning the sacred things. And what is done unto glory of God must have been released from charges of human-pleasing; for thus the victim would be truly unleavened and sacred. And portion and food for the priests is the leftover of the sacrifice. Every male is eaten in a holy place; the being spent of the sacred things in a holy place by the priests keeping reverence for our more mystical words; and the every male eating under-showing gracefully that softness is some unbeautiful thing and truly unholy for those chosen by God. For it finishes unhallowed, and sets out from spiritual blessing, and shows without share of the things from God apportioned to the saints (Leviticus 6:14–18) (1 Corinthians 7:32–34) (Matthew 6:2–6) (Matthew 6:16–18) (1 Corinthians 6:9–10)
translator_notes: Ends mid ἐκνενεμη into §24 μένων ἀγαθῶν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Judas soft for gain; priest’s perpetual fine-flour whole-burnt; pan / oil / fragments
english: Cyril: …of goods. And Judas also was softened, inclining away unto shameful-gain; and this from unmanly and ignoble reasoning; in this way also he has remained untasting of the goods from God, and wholly without share of the things gifted to the saints.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: And of the sacrifice from the herd, this is the law; yet in another manner he has ordered the from sacred race to be brought near saying: ‘This is the gift of Aaron and of his sons, which they will bring to Lord in the day in which you should anoint him, the tenth of the ephah of fine flour unto a sacrifice continually, the half of it in the morning, and the half of it in the evening. Upon a pan in oil it will be made; mixed he will bring it, rolled things, a sacrifice from fragments, a sacrifice unto a smell of fragrance to Lord. The anointed priest the one instead of him from his sons will make it; eternal law, everything will be finished; and every sacrifice of a priest will be whole-burnt, and will not be eaten.’ (Leviticus 6:19–23) So then observe, O Palladius, the accuracy of the law, and the very thin unto sacred-fitting safety. For since he ordered the sacrifices of the herd-things must not be whole-burnt, inasmuch as not having altogether holy life, but shared as it were to God and world, reasonably distinguishing, and setting in the overlying share those chosen unto sacred-work, he said the sacrifice over them must be made whole-burnt, burning down the fine flour brought near to God morning and evening, that is, through every day and in every time. For somehow always holy and having unending the fragrance—clearly the spiritual—is the chosen one, not shared to God and world, according to some, but well-sitting and undistracted, and whole from whole lying upon his own Master, and as it were crying up: ‘I have been crucified-with Christ; and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.’ (Galatians 2:20) So then the tenth of the fine flour would be a sign of life fragrancing to God according to every time. But ‘upon a pan,’ he says, and indeed ‘also mixed with oil, and from fragments he will bring it up’ (Psalm 51:17); the pan, as I at least think, under-signaling the painful, and the being mixed with oil the abundant in cheerfulness, and the from fragments the as it were tender and easily-broken of the saints’ heart enigmatically. For wholly there will follow the altogether and completely holy life, the needing to be in pains, and the ample in the hope from God, and the thoroughly easily-broken; for least fitting would be the unrubbed. For it has been written that ‘A heart crushed and humbled God will not despise.’ (Job 41:24) And fixed as a stone, and as an anvil not beaten, is the devil’s heart; for the sacred Writing says thus. And the law also extends unto all, being fulfilled by the successions of those priesting; for one must follow the of those who went before
translator_notes: Ends mid προλαβόν into §25 των εὐδοκιμήσεσι; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Imitate fathers’ whole-burnt; sin offering = Emmanuel; church mystery leftovers
english: Cyril: …ones’ well-reputations, and be shown imitators of the fathers’ good-fame, going according to track of their worship, and bringing near the fragrance most dear to God, not sharedly, but wholly. For this, I think, is the, ‘Every sacrifice of a priest will be whole-burnt.’ (Leviticus 6:24–29)
Palladius: So then we will bring ourselves near, and will be dedicated unto a smell of fragrance to God, tracking the life of the saints, and following their sacred-works, clearly the spiritual.

Cyril: Very much so, O Palladius. Yet that the rubbing-off pollution, and running through sin, would not otherwise become and exist in some, except through Christ alone, in whom and through whom is every cleansing, who endured the saving slaughter over us, one would learn, and not unto long, through the neighboring and yoked ordinance; for it holds thus: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin; in a place where they will slaughter the whole-burnt, they will slaughter the things concerning the sin before Lord; Holy of holies it is. The priest bringing it up will eat it; in a holy place it will be eaten, in the court of the tent of the witness. Everyone touching its meats will be sanctified; and for whom if there should be sprinkled from its blood upon the garment, whoever should be sprinkled upon it, will be washed in a holy place; and an earthen vessel in which if it should be boiled will be crushed; and if in a bronze vessel it should be boiled, he will rub it out, and rinse with water. Every male among the priests will eat them; Holy of holies it is to Lord.’ (John 1:29) So then the victim concerning the sin would be nothing other beside Emmanuel, who is the true lamb the one taking up the sins of the world. And he is slaughtered in the place of the whole-burnt; for Christ is not partially and according to us holy (for he did not do sin), but wholly fragrant and sacred, and supplier of sanctification to all the others. For even if he was reckoned among the lawless and became numbered with the condemned economically; yet the Father knows the death of the Son being holy and sacred. In this way he says: ‘In a place where they will slaughter the whole-burnt, they will slaughter also the concerning sin; Holy of holies it is.’ (Isaiah 53:12) For just as God of gods is the Son, thus also Holy of holies, himself sanctifying the whole creation by his own spirit, inasmuch as he has been born from Father, and is God truly. And the priest bringing it near will eat the sacrifice, he says. For each, I think, of those led unto the sacred liturgy will harvest the fruits of his own labors, and will reap the counter-gift of his own liturgy. And the leftover of the sacrifice is eaten in holy places, and in the court of the holy tent. For the mystical things are brought near in churches, and the select race of the holy table of Christ is deemed worthy in them. And wherever a lawful priest priests, a place will be holy. And the sacrifice sanctifies the one touching, and the sprinkling of the blood. We approach (2 Corinthians 5:21) (Hebrews 13:10)
translator_notes: Ends mid Προσ into §26 ίεμεν; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Approach for holy Christ; trespass ram; inwards to God; priest’s skin wage begins
english: Cyril: …for we approach the holy things, for no other grace, than so as to share the holy Christ through the unspeakable and spiritual sacrifice. And the vessels serving the sacrifices are also thoroughly cleansed, so that they may not become for some other, nor may the things having liturgized for the sacred be carried under to humans’ needs. And the law has been kept, and is saved in churches. And that being blessed is fitting for those playing-the-man, the law will clarify again saying: ‘Every male among the priests will eat them.’ (Leviticus 6:30)
Palladius: Clear is the word.

Cyril: And he legislates besides, also how the manner of the sacrifice would become well, the over sin, I mean; and which things from it are edible for those liturgizing, and which again have been excepted unto a smell of fragrance. For it has been written thus: ‘And all, he says, the things concerning the sin, of which if from their blood should be brought into the tent of the witness to propitiate in a holy place, will not be eaten, will be burned down in fire. And this is the law of the ram concerning the trespass, Holy of holies it is; in a place where they will slaughter the whole-burnt, they will slaughter the ram concerning the trespass before Lord. And he will pour the blood upon the base of the altar in a circle; and all its fat he will bring near from it, and the loin, and all the fat covering the inwards, and all the fat upon the inwards; and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them the upon the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver with the kidneys, he will take them around, and the priest will bring them up upon the altar a fruit to the Lord; concerning trespass it is. Every male from the priests will eat them, in a holy place they will eat them. Holy of holies it is. Just as the concerning the sin, thus also the concerning the trespass; one law of them the priest whoever will propitiate in it, for him it will be.’ (Leviticus 7:1–7) For he denies that the inwards of the victims must be made foods. For they must, he says, be dedicated to God alone, and be brought near to him; for this I think the, ‘will be burned down in fire,’ (Ephesians 5:2) makes clear, that is, let what has been clearly apportioned in only the divine and beyond-all nature, of which fire is unto a type, be dedicated. And with the ram of the trespass being sacrificed, the blood is poured upon the base of the altar; for holy and sacred is the death of Christ, and indeed also fragrant. For the inwards are brought up, fat, and kidneys, and lobe of the liver. And these would be, I think, just as I also said in others, unto a type of virtue not of one, but as in form of many. For as many as are most the manners of virtue; so then we have been justified in Christ, who endured the death over us, and dedicated himself unto a smell of fragrance to God and Father; and that we will not liturgize to God without wage, he clarifies, saying straightway and next: ‘And the priest bringing near whole-burnt offerings of a human, the skin of the whole-burning which he himself offers, for him will be, and every sacrifice which will be made in the oven. And every which will be made (Leviticus 7:8)
translator_notes: Ends mid ποιηθήσεται into §27 ἐπ' ἐσχάρας; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Equal shares for priests; praise offering on leavened bread; cup of salvation
english: Cyril: …upon a grate, or upon a pan, of the priest offering it, of him will be. And every sacrifice worked-up in oil, and not worked-up, for all the sons of Aaron will be; for each the equal.’ This law also is saved in churches, and awards equality to the sacred-workers, distributing to each unalterably the prizes of the bloodless sacrifice. And knowing this Paul writes: ‘Thus also the Lord ordered, those sitting-near the altar, to live from the altar.’ (Leviticus 7:9–10) And those offering the sacrifices are partners of the altar, just as again he somewhere says.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: And he again rhythms the sacrifice of praise, and pledges how it would become, saying: ‘This is the law of a sacrifice of salvation, which they will bring to Lord: If concerning praise he should offer it, he will also bring upon the sacrifice of the praise, six breads of fine flour worked-up with oil, and unleavened flatbreads smeared in oil, and fine flour mixed in oil. Upon leavened breads he will bring his gifts upon a sacrifice of praise of salvation; and he will bring near one from all his gifts, a taking-away to Lord. For the priest pouring the blood of the salvation, for him it will be; and the meats of a sacrifice of praise of salvation, for him will be. And in which day he gifts, it will be eaten; they will not leave from it unto morning.’ (1 Corinthians 9:13) He has ordered the sacrifice of the praise to be made upon leavened breads; and yet clearly and manifestly in others having said that ‘Every leaven and every honey you will not bring to Lord your God. A gift of firstfruit you will bring them to Lord; but upon the altar it will not be set up unto a smell of fragrance to Lord.’ (1 Corinthians 10:18) So then, O Palladius, do you not say the curious in these is beneficial?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then what will be the manner of the economy, come let us say, investigating as possible, and sending a path the hidden. So then most lawfully also all-divine David striking up the spiritual lyre, ‘A cup,’ he says, ‘of salvation I will take, and the name of Lord I will call upon’ (Leviticus 7:11–15); clearly calling the sacrifice of the praise a cup of salvation. And we also bring near the praise according to multitude in churches, unto oneness of spirit, and as having been brought together into one body and one soul through the faith; for it has been written that ‘And of the multitude of those having believed the heart and the soul was one.’ (Leviticus 2:11–12) And we make the glorifyings also often each quieting a house, both in day and in night; and the matter is in practice for the fair. Or is what I say not true?
Palladius: For how not?

Cyril: But whether then in churches according to multitude the victim should be brought near by us, or whether then it should be done in other places, and somehow each one, or also somehow according to two, and three, and still more, undistinguished is the standing of those accustomed to hymn-speak, and having run together unto this; for together with those already cleansed through the holy baptism, he brings up-with the victim (Psalm 116:13) (Acts 4:32);
translator_notes: Ends mid τὸ θῦμα· into §28 καὶ ὁ κατηχούμενος; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Catechumen with leavened; perfect with unleavened; oil of cheer; eat same day
english: Cyril: …and the still catechumen, and having set up-with the perfect the praise, departs from the still more mystical, and is barred from the sacrifice upon Christ. In this way well the law was pre-voicing the economy, and ordered the sacrifice of the praise to be made upon leavened breads, and in unleavened flatbreads. Each of the named, as I at least think, under-signaling a form of life; for the leavened bread will be a type of life and living not yet cleansed through the holy baptism, nor indeed altogether released from worldly uncleanness; and unleavened flatbread, of the already wiped in Christ through faith, of the perfect, I say, to whom also all-divine Paul was addressing, saying: ‘So that we may feast, not in old leaven, nor in leaven of badness and wickedness, but in unleavened of sincerity and truth.’ (1 Corinthians 5:7–8) And again: ‘Clean out then the old leaven, in order that you may be a new batch, just as you are unleavened.’ (Psalm 50:14–15)
Palladius: You spoke best.

Cyril: And fine flour besides not yet brought together unto oneness, just as also somehow in bread and in flatbread, but remaining as it were still in grains, under-hints the as one according to each and according to each one of those bringing near the praise; for we are acceptable to God, making the glorifyings, both each in part, and as one all according to multitude. And the oil is poured upon the sacrifice of the praise, under-signaling the cheerful of the matter, and that wholly and entirely the needing to be mercied by God will follow for those accustomed to bring it near. ‘For sacrifice,’ (Isaiah 49:9) he says, ‘to God a sacrifice of praise, and give back to the Highest your prayers; and call upon me in a day of your affliction, and I will rescue you, and you will glorify me.’ (James 5:13) And somewhere also the disciple of Christ writes: ‘Is someone among you depressed? Let him pray; is he cheerful? Let him psalm.’ (Exodus 15:1) So then in leavened breads, and in unleavened flatbreads, and still in millet-grains of fine flour the sacrifice of the praise needing to be worked out, he typed clearly; and with one from each being brought near, and as in one handful of the fine flour, and a sheep being slaughtered, and the inwards being sacrificed according to the law, the remaining edible for those ordered to sacred-work, the law showing the priesthood not without gain; he further orders saying: ‘In which day it is gifted, it will be eaten; they will not leave from it unto morning.’ (Psalm 96:1) Through which again it comes upon one to think somehow that; for with the time having driven past, and the present age having gone by just as a day, another manner of glorifying will be invented for us beside those we know. For just as having been freed from the dynasty upon Pharaoh rejoicing in law they were saying, ‘Let us sing to the Lord; for gloriously he has been glorified; horse and rider he threw into sea.’ (Psalm 47:5) And viewing beforehand in spirit the achievements of our Savior’s sojourn incomparably brighter and overlying, some of the saints have cried through: ‘Sing to the Lord a new song;’ and this was, ‘God went up in a shout,’ having stripped Hades, ‘and saying
translator_notes: Ends mid εἰπὼν into §29 τοῖς ἐν δεσμοῖς; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Future fuller praise; priest firstfruits and sin-portions; redemption of firstborn begins
english: Cyril: …to those in bonds, Come out, and to those in the dark, Be uncovered;’ the same manner, I think, with death having been abolished, and sin having been loosed altogether, there will be a manner of praise fitting the time; for upon greater things we will hymn; and having grown rich the goods beyond mind and word, with brighter well-speakings we will crown-together Christ the giver of all the goods for us with God and Father. ‘For whether prophecies will be abolished,’ (Isaiah 49:9) he says, ‘or knowledge will cease; And now at least we know from part; but whenever the perfect should come, the from part will be abolished.’ (1 Corinthians 13:8–10) And indeed also Christ himself somewhere said: ‘These things in parables I have spoken to you. But an hour comes when neither in parables will I speak to you, but with frankness concerning the Father I will announce to you.’ (John 16:25) So then with more perfect knowledge about to be in us according to times, higher than now we will also hymn.
Palladius: Persuasive is the word.

Cyril: So then having legislated for each sacrifice the bound fitting it, and having said very well how it would become, at once he sets the sacred-worker as partner of the altar. For it has been written thus: ‘And the Lord said toward Aaron, saying: You and your sons, and the house of your patriarchy, will take the firstfruits of the holy things; and you and your sons will take the sins of your priesthood.’ (Numbers 18:1–17) And having added to these that they must hold the sacred zeals with awakened and sober mind, ‘And behold I,’ he says, ‘have given you the keeping of the firstfruits from all the things sanctified to me from the sons of Israel; to you I have given them unto a prize, and to your sons after you, eternal lawful; and let this be for you from the sanctified holy of the fruitings, from all their gifts, and from all their sacrificings, and from every trespass of them, and from all their sins, as many as they give back to me from all the holy things, for you will be and for your sons. In the Holy of holies you will eat them; every male will eat them, you and your sons. Holy they will be for you. And this will be for you of firstfruits of their gifts, from all the puttings-on of the sons of Israel. To you I have given them and to your sons and to your daughters with you, eternal lawful; every clean one in your house will eat them. Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine, and of grain, their firstfruit as many as they should give to the Lord, to you I have given them. All the first-borns as many as in their land, as many as they should bring to Lord, for you will be. Every clean one in your house will eat them. Every having been anathematized in sons of Israel, for you will be, and every opening womb from every flesh, as many as they offer to Lord, from human until beast, for you will be. But either by ransoms the firstborn of humans will be ransomed, and the firstborn of the unclean beasts you will ransom; and his ransom, from a month-old; the valuation five shekels, according to the holy shekel, twenty obols they are; except firstborn
translator_notes: Ends mid πρωτότοκα into §30 μόσχων; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Unredeemed clean firstborn; sin named sacrifice; salt covenant; household shares
english: Cyril: …of calves and firstborn of sheep, and firstborn of goats you will not ransom; holy they are; and their blood you will pour toward the altar, and the fat you will bring up a fruit unto a smell of fragrance to Lord. And the meats will be for you, just as also the breast of the putting-on; and according to the right shoulder, for you will be. Every taking-away of the holy things, as many as if the sons of Israel should take away to Lord, I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you, eternal lawful; a covenant of eternal salt it is before Lord, for you and for your seed after you.’ So then you understand from here also, I somehow think, and very clearly, that every form of sacrifice and bringing-near he has clearly apportioned to the sacred and chosen race, and the things from every trespass, and from all the sins, that is, the victims over every trespass and sin. For a name for the victims over sin is sin. Therefore also wise Paul for us was setting the legal word upon Christ saying: ‘We beg over Christ, be reconciled to God; for the one not having known sin, he made sin over us.’ (Numbers 18:17–19) For the Son has been sacrificed over our sins, according to the Scriptures, as a harmless lamb. And that sin has been set as a name by the law for the victims over our sins, God will clarify saying through the prophet concerning the sacred-workers: ‘They will eat sins of my people;’ (Hosea 4:8) that is, the things over sins of my people will be food for the priests. So then he apportions to them leftover of every sacrifice, and orders them to be made edible, yet in a holy place, he says, and by every male. And what the word upon this is, has been said by us. And in the already gone-by, firstfruit of oil, and of grain and wine, and the ransomings of the firstborn, and indeed the dedications no longer edible for males alone, nor in the holy court, but thereafter in a priest’s house, and set for enjoyment also for the daughters themselves, and for every acquaintance and most household. And necessary unto observance is the distinction; for the leftovers of the sacrifices would be fitting for use of the sanctified alone, and will not be as common food; and a holy place, the one fitting them. english: Cyril: …you will bring salt to Lord your God.’ And the sacrifice was being sprinkled with salts, the type signaling that one must be consecrated to God thoughtfully, and as it were make the approach most tasty for him. For sometimes the mind goes off toward the unbeautiful not having to walk-straight, and the sacred things fall through, and the things done are no longer in world, but have been scattered as it were from the straight road; which indeed having suffered, necessity to collide with God, and to endure bitter justices of the easiness. So then to be awake is necessary, shaking off drunkennesses, the from worldly care. This indeed the Savior himself also persuades to do, saying: ‘Take heed lest ever your hearts be weighed with care and worldly cares.’ (Matthew 5:13) And what would be by us the manner of the sobriety, or how we will remain both unprofane and clean and outside justice, he under-signaled at once. ‘For distinguish,’ (Galatians 3:24) he says, ‘between holy and profane, and clean and unclean; and you will bring-together the sons of Israel all the lawfulls which the Lord spoke in hand of Moses.’ (Leviticus 10:9–11) And this is clearly to say that, that it is fitting for the priests shaking off the being drunk, to depart from men not holy, but profane and unclean.
